quests.sentence: I have three brothers my brother who lives in Denver is visiting this week
quests.correctAnswer: I have three brothers. My brother who lives in Denver is visiting this week.
quests.hint: Since there's more than one brother, the detail about Denver becomes essential to know which one is visiting.
quests.explanation: With multiple brothers, the clause 'who lives in Denver' is necessary to identify which brother is meant, so no commas are used.

quests.sentence: I have only one brother my brother who lives in Denver is visiting this week
quests.correctAnswer: I have only one brother. My brother, who lives in Denver, is visiting this week.
quests.hint: Since there's only one brother, the detail about Denver is just extra information, not something needed to identify him.
quests.explanation: With only one brother, the clause is nonessential extra detail and is set off with commas on both sides.

quests.sentence: She owns two cars her car that is parked outside needs new tires
quests.correctAnswer: She owns two cars. Her car that is parked outside needs new tires.
quests.hint: Since she owns more than one car, this detail is needed to identify exactly which car is meant.
quests.explanation: With two cars, the restrictive clause 'that is parked outside' is essential to specify which car, so no commas are used.

quests.sentence: I invited my parents Lady Gaga and Beyonce
quests.correctAnswer: I invited my parents, Lady Gaga, and Beyonce.
quests.hint: Without a comma before 'and,' this sentence could confusingly suggest that your parents are named Lady Gaga and Beyonce.
quests.explanation: Adding the final comma before 'and' (the Oxford comma) makes clear that three separate guests are invited, not that the parents are being renamed.

quests.sentence: This book is dedicated to my parents Ayn Rand and God
quests.correctAnswer: This book is dedicated to my parents, Ayn Rand, and God.
quests.hint: Without the final comma, this sentence could strangely suggest that Ayn Rand and God are the writer's parents.
quests.explanation: The Oxford comma before 'and' clarifies that the dedication includes three separate parties: the parents, Ayn Rand, and God.

quests.sentence: For breakfast she had eggs toast and orange juice
quests.correctAnswer: For breakfast, she had eggs, toast, and orange juice.
quests.hint: Even in a simple list like this, the final comma before 'and' keeps each item clearly separate.
quests.explanation: The Oxford comma before 'and' avoids any ambiguity about whether the last two items are meant as one combined item.

quests.sentence: Lets eat Grandma
quests.correctAnswer: Let's eat, Grandma!
quests.hint: Without a comma, this sentence could alarmingly suggest eating Grandma herself instead of inviting her to eat.
quests.explanation: The comma before the direct address 'Grandma' makes clear she's being invited to eat, not that she's the meal.

quests.sentence: I love cooking my family and my pets
quests.correctAnswer: I love cooking, my family, and my pets.
quests.hint: Without commas, this sentence could strangely suggest that cooking family and pets is the activity being described.
quests.explanation: The commas separate three different things the speaker loves, rather than implying that family and pets are being cooked.

quests.sentence: Only some students studied the students who studied passed the exam
quests.correctAnswer: Only some students studied. The students who studied passed the exam.
quests.hint: Since only some students studied, this clause narrows down exactly which students passed.
quests.explanation: Because only some students studied, the restrictive clause 'who studied' is essential to identify which students are meant, so no commas are used.

quests.sentence: She has one brother my brothers car is in the shop
quests.correctAnswer: She has one brother. My brother's car is in the shop.
quests.hint: Since there's only one brother, the apostrophe goes before the s to show singular possession.
quests.explanation: With only one brother, the possessive form is 'brother's,' with the apostrophe before the s.

quests.sentence: She has three brothers her brothers business is doing well
quests.correctAnswer: She has three brothers. Her brothers' business is doing well.
quests.hint: Since there are multiple brothers who share this business, the apostrophe goes after the s.
quests.explanation: With three brothers owning the business together, the plural possessive 'brothers'' takes the apostrophe after the s.

quests.sentence: The company changed its policy after the complaint
quests.correctAnswer: The company changed its policy after the complaint.
quests.hint: Since the policy belongs to the company, no apostrophe is used, unlike the contraction 'it's' for 'it is.'
quests.explanation: Leaving out the apostrophe in 'its' correctly shows possession; adding one would wrongly turn it into the contraction for 'it is.'

quests.sentence: The so called expert gave us advice
quests.correctAnswer: The so-called "expert" gave us advice.
quests.hint: Putting quotation marks around this word signals doubt about whether the person truly deserves that title.
quests.explanation: Quotation marks used this way, sometimes called scare quotes, suggest skepticism about the accuracy of the word, rather than presenting it as a neutral fact.

quests.sentence: He called the plan foolproof but it clearly wasnt
quests.correctAnswer: He called the plan "foolproof," but it clearly wasn't.
quests.hint: Quoting this specific word signals that the writer disagrees with calling the plan that.
quests.explanation: Placing the word in quotation marks distances the writer from the claim, implying they don't necessarily agree with the label.

quests.sentence: The company promised fast shipping which turned out to take three weeks
quests.correctAnswer: The company promised "fast" shipping, which turned out to take three weeks.
quests.hint: Quoting this word suggests the writer doubts it was truly fast at all.
quests.explanation: The quotation marks around 'fast' signal irony, implying the shipping was anything but fast.

quests.sentence: The proposal and this is the important part will save the company millions
quests.correctAnswer: The proposal—and this is the important part—will save the company millions.
quests.hint: This aside is meant to be the main point of emphasis, not a quiet afterthought.
quests.explanation: Em dashes emphasize this crucial point strongly, while parentheses would have wrongly minimized it as a minor aside.

quests.sentence: The proposal a minor detail worth mentioning will save the company millions
quests.correctAnswer: The proposal (a minor detail worth mentioning) will save the company millions.
quests.hint: This aside is meant to be downplayed as minor, not emphasized.
quests.explanation: Parentheses de-emphasize this detail as minor, matching the intended meaning that it's not the main point.

quests.sentence: The witness and this shocked the courtroom changed her entire story
quests.correctAnswer: The witness—and this shocked the courtroom—changed her entire story.
quests.hint: This reaction is meant to hit hard, not be tucked away quietly.
quests.explanation: Em dashes give this dramatic reaction the strong emphasis the sentence intends, rather than minimizing it.

quests.sentence: The report which I finished last night is on your desk
quests.correctAnswer: The report, which I finished last night, is on your desk.
quests.hint: Since there's only one report being discussed, this detail is necessary to set apart, not just a stylistic choice.
quests.explanation: Because there's only one report, the nonessential clause must be marked with commas; this isn't optional, it reflects the sentence's actual meaning.

quests.sentence: The weather today was cold and windy
quests.correctAnswer: The weather today was cold and windy.
quests.hint: Check whether two separate independent clauses are really being joined here, or just two describing words.
quests.explanation: Since 'cold and windy' are simply two adjectives describing one subject, no comma is needed at all, and adding one would be a genuine error, not a style choice.

quests.sentence: She left early and quietly slipped out
quests.correctAnswer: She left early and quietly slipped out.
quests.hint: One subject is performing this action described by two words joined by 'and' - check if a comma truly belongs here.
quests.explanation: Since 'early' and 'quietly' both describe the same single action by one subject, no comma is needed; this is a grammatical fact, not a matter of style.

quests.sentence: The panda eats shoots and leaves
quests.correctAnswer: The panda eats shoots and leaves.
quests.hint: Without any comma, this sentence describes what the panda eats: young bamboo shoots and leaves.
quests.explanation: With no comma, 'shoots and leaves' are both objects of 'eats,' describing the panda's diet.

quests.sentence: The panda eats then it shoots and leaves the area
quests.correctAnswer: The panda eats; then it shoots and leaves the area.
quests.hint: This time, the panda performs a separate independent action afterward, which calls for a stronger mark than a comma alone.
quests.explanation: Since 'the panda eats' and 'then it shoots and leaves the area' are both independent clauses, a semicolon connects them instead of a comma alone.

quests.sentence: Most of the time travelers worry about their luggage
quests.correctAnswer: Most of the time, travelers worry about their luggage.
quests.hint: Without a comma, this sentence could strangely suggest 'time travelers' are worried about luggage.
quests.explanation: The comma after 'time' clarifies that the phrase means 'most of the time,' not that the travelers themselves travel through time.

quests.sentence: I have two roommates besides Alex and Jordan I want to thank my roommates Alex and Jordan
quests.correctAnswer: I have two roommates besides Alex and Jordan. I want to thank my roommates, Alex, and Jordan.
quests.hint: Since Alex and Jordan are different people from the two roommates, the commas need to clearly separate all three groups of thanks.
quests.explanation: The Oxford comma before 'and' makes clear that the roommates, Alex, and Jordan are three separate people being thanked, not that the roommates are named Alex and Jordan.

quests.sentence: She has one dog her dog which just turned two loves to swim
quests.correctAnswer: She has one dog. Her dog, which just turned two, loves to swim.
quests.hint: Since there's only one dog, this detail about turning two is extra information, not something needed to identify the dog.
quests.explanation: With only one dog, the clause is nonessential and set off with commas on both sides.

quests.sentence: The critic called the film a masterpiece though few agreed
quests.correctAnswer: The critic called the film a "masterpiece," though few agreed.
quests.hint: Quoting this word signals doubt about whether the film truly deserves that label.
quests.explanation: The quotation marks around 'masterpiece' imply skepticism, especially combined with the fact that few people agreed.

quests.sentence: Help me finish Jason
quests.correctAnswer: Help me finish, Jason!
quests.hint: Without a comma, this sentence could alarmingly suggest 'finishing' Jason rather than asking for his help.
quests.explanation: The comma before the direct address 'Jason' clarifies he's being asked to help, not that he's the object being finished.

quests.sentence: The museum has one guide our guide who has worked there for decades knows every exhibit
quests.correctAnswer: The museum has one guide. Our guide, who has worked there for decades, knows every exhibit.
quests.hint: Since there's only one guide, the detail about decades of experience is extra information, not something needed to identify the guide.
quests.explanation: With only one guide, the clause is nonessential and set off with commas on both sides.

quests.sentence: The reviewer described the restaurant as authentic despite it serving frozen meals
quests.correctAnswer: The reviewer described the restaurant as "authentic," despite it serving frozen meals.
quests.hint: Quoting this word suggests real doubt about whether the restaurant deserves that description.
quests.explanation: The quotation marks around 'authentic' signal skepticism, reinforced by the contrasting detail about frozen meals.
